plates.title: Cargo Cult Science — Overview
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, vellum-toned with a gilt border of vines, divided into a vertical chain of small framed vignettes running top to bottom in strict reading order, each with a lettered caption beneath it in capitals and nothing else written anywhere on the page. At top, THE COMMENCEMENT ADDRESS: a robed speaker at a lectern before gowned graduates. Below, THE RHINOCEROS HORN: a medieval apothecary holds up a curved horn to a doubtful customer. The chain forks into three vignettes side by side inside a loosely drawn enclosure labeled only by its scene (no words): THE ISOLATION TANK — a man floating in a dark sealed tank; NO PROGRESS ON CRIME — a barred cell with theorists outside holding scrolls; and beneath those two, converging, THE COCKTAIL-PARTY TEST — a hostess leaning toward two guests at a party. The three funnel down into CARGO CULT NAMED: an islander in a straw hut with bamboo headphones, watching an empty runway lined with fires. From there the chain narrows again: REPORTING AGAINST YOURSELF — a scholar at a desk setting two opposing scrolls side by side; this forks to THE OIL MERCHANT'S CLAIM — a merchant holding up an oil bottle before a crowd — and to THE CREEPING MEASUREMENT — a rising staircase of scales each set higher than the last, which leads down into THE CREEPING MEASUREMENT feeding TIME REVEALS THE TRUTH — a sundial over old papers. These converge into NOT FOOLING YOURSELF — a scholar holding a mirror to his own face. The chain continues to SKIPPING THE OLD TEST, inside a second loose enclosure — a student at a lab bench with a rat and maze reaching past the old test. Finally at the bottom, THE CLOSING WISH: a lone scholar walking through an open gate into open country. Render all in brown ink and faded gold leaf, with thin red connecting lines linking each vignette frame to the next, vines and small birds filling any empty margin but never crowding the scenes, which should be large enough to read clearly across the width of the page.

plates.title: Searching For What Doesn't Work
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page continuing the same brown-ink and gold-leaf register, framed by a vine border, showing a vertical chain of labeled vignettes with captions lettered beneath each and no other writing on the page. At top, SEPARATING THE IDEAS: a hand shaking a sieve full of medieval charms, some falling through. Below, UFOS AND ASTROLOGY: small floating symbols — a saucer shape, a star-chart, a swirling cloud — above a crowd looking up. The chain leads to ESALEN RETREAT: a cliffside building over the sea with robed figures on its terraces, from which two smaller framed scenes branch off to the side: THE TOE AND THE PITUITARY, showing a man pressing a woman's toe on a massage table while a bemused bystander in a bath looks on, and THE UNBENT KEY, showing two men rubbing a key under running water with no effect. Below the retreat scene, the main chain continues to READING SCORES STALL: a classroom of children with a flat or falling line on a chalkboard. This leads to THE INTIMIDATED TEACHER: a teacher holding a book, dwarfed by a tall stack of looming rule-ledgers. Next, THE SUSPICIOUS WIFE: a woman glancing sharply across a party room at two guests in conversation. Finally at the bottom, PSYCHOTHERAPY ON TRIAL: a patient reclining on a couch with a note-taker seated beside them, both small and distant as if under question. Thin red connecting lines link each vignette in sequence top to bottom; vines, small birds and faded gold leaf fill the margins without crowding the scenes, which should be large and clear across the width of the page.

plates.title: Case Studies In Poor Science
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page in the same brown-ink, gold-leaf register as the previous plates, bordered with vines, showing a vertical sequence of small framed vignettes each captioned beneath in capitals, with no other lettering on the page. At top, PROPOSING TO SKIP A STEP: a student pointing to a maze marked Y with rats already inside. Beside it, REPEAT THE OLD RUN FIRST: a robed figure gesturing toward an older maze marked X. Below, two small scenes branch from this: DEEMED A WASTE OF TIME, a professor waving a dismissive hand, and BORROWED COMPARISON DATA, a physicist at a large apparatus comparing his readings to a chart borrowed from elsewhere. The chain continues downward into a longer enclosed group of scenes about the maze experiment: THE CORRIDOR OF DOORS, a long row of identical doors with a rat running to the one that had food before; PAINTING THE DOORS ALIKE, a hand matching the texture of two doors while the rat still finds its way; THE SOUND IN THE FLOOR, a rat's footsteps on a wooden floor with sound-waves sketched rising, sand being poured ahead; and THE TRUE CLUE FOUND, a man standing over a sand-floored corridor watching the rat finally choose at random. From this the chain forks to two final scenes side by side at the bottom: THE SHRINKING ESP EFFECT, a row of result-cards fading one after another into blankness while a figure watches, and TRAINING ONLY THE HITTERS, an instructor picking a few students from a line and turning the rest away. Thin red lines connect each vignette in sequence, vines and small birds filling the margins lightly without crowding the scenes, which should be drawn large and clear across the width of the page.
